texts.preamble: Smt. Jannu Alekya vs The State Of Telangana on 15 September, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt Justice K. Sujana Writ Petition No.25672 of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: 2. This Writ Petition is filed to issue Writ of Habeas Corpus to declare the detention order vide C.No.560/WRL/ CSB/XI/2023, dated 23-08-2023 issued by respondent No.3 whereby and whereunder detaining the husband of the petitioner by name Mr.Jannu Anil Kumar including all consequential orders as the same as illegal, arbitrary, improper, unilateral, unconstitutional and violative of Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution of India and to forthwith release the detenu. 3. Impugned detention order was passed relying on two ground cases i.e., Crime Nos.10 and 11 of 2023 pending on the file on Inthezargunj Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 468, 471, 386, 392 and 506 r/w.34 of IPC. The allegations leveled against detenu are that he along with Mr.Samala Raja Ram Mohan and others created fake documents and claiming ownership over the subject property. Therefore, he is a land grabber. 4. Detaining authority also referred Crime No.74 of 2022 pending on the file of very same Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 419 and 420 r/w.34 of IPC. In the said crime also the allegation is same. There is no mention about the details of alleged associates of the detenu in all the three cases. 5. In the impugned detention order itself there is mention about pendency of following suits: 6. In the impugned detention order there is also mention about settlement of suits before the Lok Adalath. The allegations leveled against the detenu are that the detenu and his associates have taken amount and settling land disputes. Therefore, according to the detaining authority, he is a Land Grabber. In view of the same, it is relevant to extract the definition of 'Land Grabber' as defined in Section 2 (j) of The Telangana Prevention Of Dangerous Activities Of Boot-Leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders And White Collar Or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 as follows: (j) "land-grabber" means a person, who illegally takes possession of any land (whether belonging to Government, local authority or any other person) or enters into or creates illegal tenancies or lease and licence, agreements or any other agreement in respect of such lands; or who constructs unauthorised structures thereon for sale or hire, or give such lands to any person on rental or lease and licence basis or for construction or use and occupation of un-authorised structures or he knowingly gives financial aid to any person for taking illegal possession of such lands, or for construction of unauthorised structures thereon or who collects or attempts to collect from any occupier of such lands, rent, compensation, or other charges by criminal intimidation or who evicts or attempts to evict any such occupier by force without resorting to the lawful procedure; or who abets in any manner the doing of any of the above mentioned things; 8. However, respondent No.2 detaining authority though referred the said Crime did not consider the same while issuing the impugned detention order.
texts.arguments: Sri Ajay Kumar Madisetti, learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that Court below granted bail to the detenu in Crime No.74 of 2022. 11. Hon'ble Apex Court in Ashok Kumar Vs. Delhi Administration 1 the Hon'ble Apex Court held that (1982) 2 SCC 403 preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it to prevent him from doing. 12. In Ram Manohar Lohia Vs. State of Bihar 2 the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows: Smt. Jannu Alekya vs The State Of Telangana on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164740136/ 2 "Does the expression "public order' take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. Other examples can be imagined. (1966) 1 SCR 709 The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". 13. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 3, the Hon'ble Supreme Court explained the phrase 'habitual criminal' as follows: "12. A person is habitual criminal who by force of-habit or inward disposition, inherent or latent in him, has grown accustomed to lead a life of crime. It is the force of habit inherent or latent in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him dangerous to the society in general. In simple language the word 'habitually' means 'by force of habit'." 14. Smt. Jannu Alekya vs The State Of Telangana on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164740136/ 3 issuing preventive detention order.
